Performers
Peter Pears (tenor), Dennis Brain (horn), Boyd Neel String Orchestra (string orchestra), Benjamin Britten (conductor) Documented

The Internet Archive creator field lists Pears, Brain and the Boyd Neel String Orchestra. The CHARM record names Britten as conductor, and Philip Stuart’s Decca discography lists Pears, Brain, the Boyd Neel String Orchestra and Britten for the session.

[1] [2] [4]
Work version
The Elegy alone, on one side of the six-side Decca set AK 1151–⁠53: side 3 of 6, matrix AR 8463. It shares a disc with the Dirge (side 4, AR 8464). Inferred, not documented

The titles of the six sides in the CHARM record and the Internet Archive items show the Elegy on a side of its own. That the side holds the whole movement is inferred from the neighbouring sides, which begin and end with other movements, and from the side’s length (4 min 21 s); no source states the movement’s duration in this recording or compares the side with the score.

[1] [2]
Recorded
1944-05-25 Inferred, not documented

Stuart’s discography records the Serenade sessions as 25 May 1944 and says that three sides (8461, 8464 and 8466) were re-made on 8 October 1944. The side transferred here is AR 8463, take 2, which is not among the re-made sides, so it is inferred to date from 25 May 1944; the discography does not say which take was issued.

[4] [1]
Place
London Inferred, not documented

The discography lists the 25 May 1944 session at West Hampstead Studios, Decca’s London studios.

[4]
Label
Decca (UK), 78 rpm Documented

The Internet Archive item gives the label as Decca and the speed as 78; Stuart’s discography lists the Serenade among Decca’s UK 78 rpm issues. The record size is not stated in the sources consulted.

[1] [2] [4]
Catalogue
Decca AK 1153 (third disc of the automatic-coupling set AK 1151–⁠53), issued in the UK in November 1945 Documented

The file name of the transfer is AK_1153_AR_8463-2. Stuart lists the issue as “(Nov45) (A)K1151-53”, and says UK release dates come from Decca’s monthly supplements or from advertisements and reviews in The Gramophone. The December 1945 issue of The Gramophone reviews the set as “Decca K1151-3 … Auto AK1151-3”. The same six sides were also issued in manual sequence as K1151–⁠53, in which the Elegy and the Dirge share K1152 (Decca advertisement, The Gramophone, February 1946); the disc transferred here is the automatic coupling AK 1153, which carries the same two sides.

[4] [5] [6] [1] [2]
Matrix, take, sides
AR 8463, take 2 (side 3 of 6); AR 8464 take 4, the Dirge, is on the other side of the same disc Documented

From the item metadata and the CHARM record, which list the six sides of the set as AR 8461-4, AR 8466-4, AR 8462-3, AR 8465-4, AR 8463-2 and AR 8464-4.

[1] [2]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

The item names no transfer engineer. It belongs to the Internet Archive’s Centre for the History and Analysis of Recorded Music (CHARM) 78rpm collection and carries a CHARM record (METS_AK_1151, created 30 January 2009 by conversion from a spreadsheet).

[1] [3] [2]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The Internet Archive upload is a copying event, not the date of the transfer; the sibling item for side 4 was added on 15 January 2019.

[1] [2]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

The item states no stylus, equalisation or noise reduction. The MP3 is the Internet Archive derivative of the uploaded FLAC.

[1]
Composition rights
In copyright. Britten died on 4 December 1976, so the Serenade is protected in the EU and the United Kingdom (life plus 70 years) until the end of 2046; Boosey & Hawkes is the publisher. Blake (1757–⁠1827) wrote the poem, which is in the public domain. Inferred, not documented

The publisher is documented by the Boosey & Hawkes page and Blake’s dates by the Sun Valley note. The term is a calculation from the composer’s death date, which the composer chapter on this site gives. Rights in the composition are separate from rights in the recording and do not block publication.

[11] [10]
Recording rights
Territorial EU and UK public domain: first published before 1963 (Decca AK 1151–⁠53, November 1945). United States status not established. Documented

The release date is Philip Stuart’s, taken from Decca’s monthly supplements or from The Gramophone; The Gramophone for December 1945 independently reviews the set as already on sale. For a recording first published in 1945 the Copyright Office describes a term of 95 years plus 5 years after first publication in the United States, to the end of 2045; whether that term applies to this British issue was not established. The item carries no licence statement and sits in the CHARM collection, not in the Great 78 Project; its metadata carries no litigation, takedown or restriction flag.

[4] [5] [12] [1]

Benjamin Britten, Serenade for Tenor, Horn and Strings, Op. 31: IV. Elegy. Peter Pears, tenor; Dennis Brain, horn; Boyd Neel String Orchestra; Benjamin Britten, conductor. Decca matrix AR 8463 take 2, London, 1944; issued as Decca AK 1153, set AK 1151–⁠53, in November 1945. Internet Archive item 78_serenade-for-tenor-horn-strings-op31-s3-elegy-blake_pears-peter-brain-d-boy, from the Centre for the History and Analysis of Recorded Music 78rpm collection. Territorial EU and UK basis (first published before 1963); US status not established. Rights statement

Accessed 2026-10-19.
